01

The brand

What Dogeared is, who it speaks to, and the single idea every decision in this document protects.

Dogeared is a quiet place to keep a reading life — not a leaderboard for one.

Product

A reading companion that times sessions, holds a private journal, recommends by taste, and turns a month of reading into something worth keeping.

Audience

Committed readers who want a record of what they read and how it landed — and who have quietly opted out of noisier social reading platforms.

Promise

Everything is optional. Nothing nags. The reader is never behind — the app has no opinion about how fast anyone should read.

The four principles

PrincipleWhat it means in practice
Quiet by defaultNo streaks that shame, no red badges, no urgency. A missed day is covered by a freeze, not punished. Notifications respect quiet hours and never repeat within three days.
Literary, not corporateThe serif does the talking. Copy sounds like a well-read friend, not a growth team. "Closing the book for now," not "End session."
Private firstData lives on the device. Cloud sync is opt-in. A journal entry is assumed unshared until the reader decides otherwise.
Monochrome disciplineBlack, white and grey. Colour appears in exactly two sanctioned places — never in the interface itself. See 05.

Naming

FormRule
DogearedOne word, capital D, no hyphen. Correct in all contexts including body copy and URLs.
Dog-earedOnly when used as the ordinary English adjective — "a dog-eared paperback." Never as the product name.
DogEared / dogearedNever. Camel case and all-lowercase are both incorrect, including in code comments and social handles where the platform allows capitals.
02

Voice & tone

Dogeared sounds like someone who reads a great deal and does not mention it. Warm, specific, unhurried, never motivational.

Write it this way

✓Say

Closing the book for now

×Not

End session

✓Say

It's been a few days — Piranesi is right where you left it.

×Not

Don't lose your streak! Read now to stay on track 🔥

✓Say

A quieter week — that's alright.

×Not

You missed your goal by 43%.

✓Say

Pressed between the pages.

×Not

Quote saved successfully!

✓Say

A few words, or a photo — something to keep.

×Not

Error: field cannot be empty.

Mechanics

Sentence case everywhere, including buttons. Em dashes over semicolons. Contractions always. One exclamation mark per quarter, at most. Emoji only in the reader's own content, never in ours.

Empty and error states

An empty screen is an invitation, not an apology: "The wishlist awaits its first temptation." Errors explain what happened and what to do — they never say sorry and never blame the reader.

03

The logo

A dog reading a book, drawn in a single confident line. It is the only mark. There is no secondary emblem and no alternate lockup.

Primary mark. Full-colour equivalent does not exist — the mark is drawn in ink on paper and reproduces identically in every medium.

Anatomy

The line

A single hand-drawn contour of uneven weight. The wobble is deliberate and must be preserved — it is what stops the brand reading as a tech logo.

The book

Held open and forward, covering most of the body. The book is the subject; the dog is the reader. Never crop the book out of frame.

The ear

One ear folds forward — the visual pun the whole brand rests on. It must remain legible at every size.

Clear space

XX

X equals the height of the folded ear. Keep a margin of at least X on all four sides, clear of type, rules, image edges and other marks. When in doubt, give it more.

Minimum sizes

Below 24 px the folded ear closes up and the mark reads as a blob. At those sizes use the wordmark instead, or nothing at all.

Placement on backgrounds

On #F3F2F7 — preferred.

On white — acceptable.

On #141414 — invert the mark.

04

Logo misuse

Each example below is a real failure seen in the wild. None of them are permitted, in any medium, for any reason.

×Never stretch or condense. Scale proportionally only.
×Never recolour. The mark is ink, never tinted.
×Never rotate or set at an angle.
×Never add shadow, glow, bevel or outline.
×Never place on a busy or low-contrast ground.
×Never crop, mask or bleed the mark off an edge.
Dogeared
×Never place the mark after the wordmark. It leads, always.
×Never reduce opacity to use the mark as a watermark.
✓Correct: unmodified, upright, generous clear space.

Colour

Dogeared has no brand colour. That is the brand. Every interface surface is drawn from a single neutral ramp, and the discipline is the point — it makes book covers the only colourful thing on screen.

The two sanctioned exceptions

Colour is permitted in exactly two places. Both are contained, both are justified, and neither appears in the interface chrome. Any third exception requires sign-off from the brand owner.

1 · Share cards anchored to one book

A gradient sampled from that book's own cover, used as the card background. It makes a shared card feel like the book rather than like the app. A fixed 30% black scrim sits over it so white type always clears 4.5:1 — including over pale or bright covers.

2 · Book covers themselves

Cover artwork is reproduced as published, never tinted, greyscaled or duotoned. The monochrome interface exists precisely so covers can carry all the colour.

Not permitted: coloured status states, coloured category tags, coloured charts, coloured illustration, gradients in the interface, or a marketing accent colour introduced for a campaign.

06

Typography

Two families, strictly divided by job. The serif carries feeling and holds the reader's own words. The sans carries the machinery — labels, controls, data.

Display · editorial
Newsreader
Extra light 200Light 300Regular 400Italic
AaBbCcDdEeFfGg  0123456789  &?!—“”
Interface · utility
Outfit
Light 300Regular 400Medium 500
AaBbCcDdEeFfGg  0123456789  &?!—“”

Newsreader is for

Headings, book titles, quotes, journal entries, the timer, big numbers, and any sentence with feeling in it. Set light — 200–300 at display sizes. Never bold.

Outfit is for

Buttons, labels, eyebrows, metadata, form fields, navigation, stat captions. Set 300–500. Never used above 24 px.

Type scale

DisplayA reading life44 / 200 / 1.05
H1 · page titleLibrary30 / 300 / 1.12
H2 · sheet titleClosing the book for now22 / 300 / 1.2
H3 · card titleThis month in numbers17.5 / 300 / 1.3
BodyTime your reading and keep a gentle streak going.15 / 300 / 1.6
Supportingacross 4 sessions13.5 / 300 / 1.5
Captionpage 214 of 38012.5 / 300 / 1.45
EyebrowWeekly report11 / 500 / .18em

The pairing in use

Weekly report · 12–18 May
412 pages this week

Across four sessions, mostly on the commute. Your longest sit-down was Thursday evening — an hour and ten minutes with Piranesi.

The eyebrow and body are Outfit; the headline and the book title are Newsreader. A book title always takes the serif, even inside a sans paragraph — titles belong to the literary voice.

Rules

01Never set Newsreader in bold. If a heading needs more weight, increase size, not weight.
02Never set Outfit above 24 px. Large sans reads as a generic SaaS product and breaks the literary register.
03Sentence case everywhere. Uppercase is reserved for eyebrows, at 0.18em tracking.
04Body copy holds to roughly 60–68 characters per line. Journal and quote text may run wider on desktop.
05Numerals in stats and timers use tabular figures so digits don't jitter as they count.
06Fallbacks are Georgia, serif and the system UI stack. Both are tested — the layout must not break when webfonts fail.
07

Iconography

Forty-four line icons drawn to one specification. They are quiet wayfinding, never decoration, and never the loudest thing on a screen.

Construction

Canvas24 × 24 units
Stroke1.7 units, uniform — no tapering
Caps & joinsRound, always
FillNone. Outline only, except the single filled favourite heart
ColourcurrentColor — icons inherit text colour, never carry their own
Live areaKeep artwork within 21 units; leave the outer ring clear

Sample of the set

Icons pair with a text label wherever the meaning is not universally obvious. An icon alone is acceptable only for back, close, search, share and settings.

08

Illustration

Six reader portraits, offered as profile avatars. They are the one place in the brand where warmth is allowed to be soft rather than restrained.

Style specification

Do

Hand-drawn contour with visible line weight variation. Soft, desaturated washes. Round, unthreatening forms. A book is present or implied in every portrait. Generous negative space so the figure survives a circular crop.

Don't

No vector-perfect geometry, no gradients or 3D shading, no saturated colour, no human faces, no corporate flat-illustration tropes. Never crop so tightly that the figure touches the circle's edge.

Why these are allowed to carry colour: the avatars are the reader's chosen stand-in, not interface chrome — the same logic that lets a book cover keep its own colour. They always appear inside a circular mask at 42–120 px. Commissioning new portraits requires matching the existing line weight and palette; the set is designed to be extended, not remixed.

09

The dog-ear

The brand's one graphic device: a folded page corner. It is the name made visible, and it is the only ornament permitted anywhere in the system.

Applied to a card

The fold sits at the top-right, cut at 45°, with a soft drop shadow beneath the lifted corner and the page's underside tinted grey at 30% opacity. It reads as paper, not as a graphic.

Specification

PositionTop-right corner, flush
Angle45°, always
Size24 px on cards · up to 68 px on covers
UndersideGrey accent at 30% opacity
Shadow2 px offset, 14% black, beneath the lift only

Where it belongs

✓Cards that hold something the reader made or kept — a journal entry, a finished book, a saved quote, a monthly recap.
✓Section markers in brand documents, as used throughout this one.
✓The cover of any long-form brand or marketing artefact.
×Never on every card at once. If more than roughly a third of the cards on a screen are folded, the device stops meaning anything.
×Never on buttons, chips, inputs, navigation, or anything interactive that isn't a card.
×Never at a different angle, on a different corner, or animated as a peel.
10

Interface

The components the brand is actually made of. Rendered here at production values — these are the live specifications, not approximations.

Buttons

Solid — one per screen, the single most likely next action. Ghost — secondary actions. Quiet — tertiary, dismissive. All pill-shaped, 11 px × 20 px padding, Outfit 300 at 13.5 px. Disabled drops to 40% opacity and loses pointer events.

Contrast note: solid buttons invert with the theme. In dark mode the fill becomes #F2F2F2 and the label #141414. Never hard-code white label text on a solid button — it disappears in dark mode.

Chips

Currently reading 380 pages Literary fiction Due back 14 May Reread ×2

Chips are labels, never buttons. The filled variant marks the active shelf or state; all others stay outlined.

Quote block

“A room without books is like a body without a soul.”
— Cicero

Serif italic, centred, with the attribution in tracked uppercase sans. When a quote comes from a specific book the title follows the author in serif italic, lower case: — George R.R. Martin, A Dance with Dragons

Elevation

Flat

Inline content. 1 px border, no shadow.

Raised

Cards on the canvas.

Lifted

Sheets, dialogs, share cards.

Two shadow tokens only. Shadows are always neutral-black at low opacity — never tinted, never coloured.

Radii & motion

Corner radii

24px large cards and sheets · 16px medium panels · 10px small elements and inputs · 99px pills and avatars. No other values.

Motion

One easing curve throughout: cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). Entrances 300–450 ms, state changes 150–200 ms. All motion is suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

11

Accessibility

Measured, not assumed. Every pairing below was calculated against WCAG 2.1 — including the one that does not pass.

AaInk on background15.26:1AAA
AaInk on surface16.09:1AAA
AaSolid button label15.26:1AAA
AaSecondary text on background4.61:1AA
AaGrey accent on background4.11:1AA large
AaTertiary text on background2.31:1Fails

Known limitation — read this before using tertiary ink. #A1A1A5 does not meet the 4.5:1 minimum for body text and must never carry information a reader needs: no error text, no field labels, no instructions, no prices, no dates that matter. It is cleared only for decorative dividers, placeholder glyphs and duplicated labels where the same information is already available at full contrast nearby. Where a designer wants tertiary ink for real content, use secondary ink instead.

Dark mode

Primary text clears 16.46:1 and secondary 6.88:1 — both comfortably above requirement. Dark-mode tertiary reaches 3.11:1 and carries the same restriction as its light counterpart.

Non-negotiables

Visible keyboard focus on every interactive element. Touch targets 44 px minimum. Icon-only controls carry a title or accessible label. Never signal state by shape or position alone — in a monochrome system there is no colour to fall back on.

Handoff

What ships with this document, and where the authoritative values live.

AssetSource of truth
Colour & type tokensCSS custom properties in css/styles.css. Every value in section 05 and 06 is taken directly from there — treat that file as authoritative if the two ever disagree.
Logoicons/logo.png — plus derived app icons at 192 px, 512 px and maskable.
Icon set44 icons as inline SVG path data in js/icons.js. Rendered through one shared helper so stroke weight and caps stay uniform.
IllustrationSix avatar portraits in icons/, referenced by the avatar preset list.
TypefacesNewsreader and Outfit, both open licence via Google Fonts. No licence fee, no seat limits, embeddable in product and print.

Before you deviate

This system is deliberately narrow. Most requests to add something — a brand colour, a second display face, a filled icon style, a peel animation — are requests to make Dogeared look like other software. If a real need can't be met within these rules, raise it with the brand owner and change the guideline rather than making a quiet exception in one screen.
